In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature and origin of the human mind.
the nature of the sign function, and its relation to language, consciousness and life.

the nature and origins of meaning, and how it is that meaning is created in and through human and animal communication, and in the process of life, in a way that is compatible with an evolutionary understanding of nature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the semiotic hierarchy, as outlined here, is a theory of meaning, which is both an ontology and a theory of evolution, where each of the four levels rests on the previous, and makes possible attainment of the next, while also being ontologically new, in the sense of emergent.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to understand how life can become language, and what is the role of signs in this process.
we are trying to understand the world from the point of view of meaning, in a way that is both scientifically rigorous and phenomenologically faithful to our own experiences.

The Semiotic Hiearchy provides a framework for understanding the emergence of life, consciousness, meaning and language in a unified way, as a process of increasing levels of semiotic organization, and that this is possible on the basis of an evolutionary, though non-standardly biosemiotic framework.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the four levels of the hierarchy, life, consciousness, signs and language, are not just different types of sign systems, but are different in kind, and that each level is necessary for the existence of the next.
meaning, in its most general sense, can be understood as the result of a semiotic process, which is both a biological and a cultural process.
the four levels of meaning can be seen as a hierarchy, where each level rests on the previous one, and makes possible a further step.
